5. The respondent No. 2 has filed an affidavit-in-opposition denying the material contention of the petitioner and stating, inter alia. that DW 1 has categorically stated before the Labour Court that the charge sheet was sent to the petitioner and that the charge sheet which was Ext. A before the Labour Court was in fact issued by the Deputy General Manager and not by Assistant Labour Officer who was in the Enquiry Committee. The Assistant Labour Officer signed the charge sheet for the Deputy General Manager. 

 7. With regard to the information that the charge-sheet was signed by a person who sat as Member Secretary of the Enquiry Committee, the Respondent No. 2 has asserted in the affidavit-in-opposition that the Assistant Labour Officer who signed the charge sheet signed it on behalf of the Deputy General Manager, who is the Chief Executive of the employer company Respondent No. 2. This assertion by the Respondent No. 2 has not been denied by the petitioner by submitting a reply to the affidavit-in-opposition. Be that as it may, it has been decided in series of cases before the Appellate Division and by this Court that in the event of any irregularity or illegality committed by the Enquiry Committee the Labour Court under section 25(1)(d) can always convert an order of dismissal into an order of termination.
